answer: Each earning key is bound to one surveyed ablation stake on a named glacier. The holder cuts an ice wafer, publishes its isotope serial, and mounts a signing logger on the bedrock ledge at the snout to timestamp melt pulses. An unannounced sampler later draws water from the glacier-fed meadow fen; the key is accepted only if the fen ion balance and the logger pulses both match that wafer. Reused stakes, borrowed wafers, or mismatched samples are slashed as one farm. Fielding N identities costs N glacier stakes, N unique wafers, and N live meadow appointments that cannot share an hour.
